team_adoption.scope: Team-adoption analysis: learning curve, training burden, adoption resistance, and change management for Brightline (40-person ad agency, Dublin)
assumptions: Headcount mix assumed: ~12 account managers (AMs), ~6 media buyers, ~14 creatives, ~8 ops/finance/leadership; no dedicated CRM admin or RevOps hire
Current state assumed: spreadsheets + Google Workspace/Slack + ad-platform UIs; no incumbent CRM to migrate from
English-speaking team, EU/GDPR jurisdiction; budget-sensitive mid-size independent agency
Pricing/feature knowledge as of early 2026; no web verification performed

salesforce.overall: Steepest. Sales Cloud assumes an admin who configures objects, page layouts, and permission sets before end users see anything sensible. Out-of-the-box it is noisy for agency workflows.
salesforce.time_to_basic_proficiency: 4-8 weeks per user; 3-6 months to confident self-serve reporting
salesforce.admin_dependency: High - realistically needs a part-time certified admin or an implementation partner (EUR 10-25k typical for SMB scoping)

hubspot.overall: Gentlest. Consumer-grade UI, opinionated defaults, free HubSpot Academy courses, and native Gmail/Outlook capture mean AMs can run a pipeline in days. HubSpot's EMEA HQ is in Dublin, so local events, support hours, and hiring-pool familiarity are unusually strong for this buyer.
hubspot.time_to_basic_proficiency: 1-2 weeks per user; 4-6 weeks to self-serve dashboards
hubspot.admin_dependency: Low - a power-user AM or ops person can administer it part-time

zoho_crm.overall: Moderate. Capable but the UI is denser and less polished; the wider Zoho One suite creates navigation sprawl and 'which app do I use?' confusion. Documentation is thinner and community answers more variable.
zoho_crm.time_to_basic_proficiency: 2-4 weeks per user; 6-10 weeks to self-serve reporting
zoho_crm.admin_dependency: Medium - configuration is approachable but fiddly; expect ongoing tinkering

learning_curve_by_role.account_managers: Heaviest users: pipeline, contacts, activity logging, renewal/retainer tracking. HubSpot's email sidekick and automatic activity capture remove most manual data entry, which is where agency CRMs usually die. Salesforce gives them more power but demands disciplined data hygiene they have never had to practise. Zoho sits between, with clunkier email sync.
learning_curve_by_role.media_buyers: Care about campaign/spend context, not deal stages. HubSpot's native ads integrations (Google, Meta, LinkedIn) surface spend-to-pipeline data without extra licences. Salesforce needs AppExchange connectors or Marketing Cloud (cost + separate learning curve). Zoho requires Zoho Marketing Automation or third-party glue. Train buyers only on read/report views, not full CRM workflows.
learning_curve_by_role.creatives: Lightest touch and highest flight risk. They should never be forced into CRM data entry; they need brief visibility and status only. Recommend zero or read-only seats for creatives on any platform, with briefs flowing to the existing PM tool via integration. This single decision removes roughly a third of the apparent training burden.

training_burden_estimate.salesforce: AMs ~24-32 hrs each (Trailhead plus instructor-led), buyers ~8 hrs, admin 100+ hrs or outsourced; ongoing admin load permanent
training_burden_estimate.hubspot: AMs ~10-14 hrs (Academy certs), buyers ~4 hrs, admin ~20 hrs setup then ~2 hrs/week
training_burden_estimate.zoho_crm: AMs ~16-20 hrs, buyers ~6 hrs, admin ~40-60 hrs setup with continued tweaking

expected_adoption_resistance.general: Ad agencies are structurally CRM-averse: senior AMs treat relationships as personal capital and data entry as unbillable overhead. Expect passive resistance (stale pipelines, deals logged after the fact) rather than open refusal. Resistance peaks at week 3-6 when novelty fades.
expected_adoption_resistance.salesforce: HIGH - perceived as 'corporate', slow first-session experience, and any config gap is read as proof the tool is wrong for agencies
expected_adoption_resistance.hubspot: LOW-MODERATE - main risk is complacency (using it as a glorified address book) rather than rejection
expected_adoption_resistance.zoho_crm: MODERATE - 'cheap tool' perception among senior staff plus UI grumbles can legitimise opting out

change_management_recommendations: Name an exec sponsor (MD or Head of Client Services) who runs the Monday pipeline meeting exclusively from the CRM from day one - meetings driven from the tool are the single strongest adoption lever
Pilot with one full account pod (1 AM lead + 2 AMs + 1 buyer) for 4 weeks before agency-wide rollout; fix friction before scaling
Appoint one champion per discipline (AM, media, ops) with 2 hrs/week protected time; in Dublin, leverage HubSpot's local user groups if HubSpot is chosen
Ruthless minimal-field policy: max 7 required fields on any record; every additional mandatory field measurably suppresses logging
Automate capture first (email/calendar sync, call logging) so the CRM fills itself before asking humans to type
Phase rollout: AMs month 1, media buyers month 2 (read/report views), creatives never - integrate briefs into the PM tool instead
Schedule paid-time Academy/Trailhead certification windows; do not ask staff to train on personal time
Set a 90-day kill-or-commit review with explicit usage KPIs: >=90% of live deals in CRM, activity logged within 24h, forecast built only from CRM data
team_adoption.recommendation_rationale: For a 40-person Dublin agency with no CRM admin, adoption risk dominates feature comparisons. HubSpot has the shortest time-to-value, the lowest training burden (~10-14 hrs per heavy user vs 24-32 for Salesforce), the lowest expected resistance, native ad-platform integrations media buyers actually need, and a Dublin-local vendor presence. Salesforce's power is unusable without admin capacity Brightline lacks; Zoho's savings are partly repaid in configuration time and softer adoption. Confidence is 4/5 rather than 5/5 because pricing/GDPR findings from sibling agents could shift the total-cost picture.
